description: Frozen Phase 0 acceptance contracts for the six reference plugins used to prove Plugin Platform v2 without promoting proposals to shipped capability.

plugins.purpose: Prove the generic SDK transcript, lifecycle, descriptor, command dispatch, cancellation, and malformed-input behavior.
acceptance: A fixed command invocation returns the frozen JSON-only result.
The process remains stopped until the command activation event.
Cancellation, crash, timeout, oversize output, and unknown methods fail closed.
Disable invalidates the process instance and all late responses.

plugins.purpose: Prove that the platform can deliver a useful non-indicator product feature with native UI, scoped data reads, settings, storage, jobs, and optional notifications.
acceptance: Install from a fixed-digest bundle and show exact read/storage scopes before enable.
Scan a bounded symbol set through the host market-data adapter without direct DataManager access.
Render a declarative side panel and optional chart markers without plugin JavaScript.
Revocation makes the next read fail and disable removes process, job, view, layer, and handles.
An update that expands symbols, history depth, or required permissions remains staged.
Rollback restores the prior version and compatible private data while v1 runtimes remain unchanged.

plugins.purpose: Prove complex custom UI through an isolated iframe and the versioned UI bridge without entering the CandleScope JavaScript realm.
acceptance: The iframe cannot access parent DOM, cookies, host storage, host JavaScript objects, or service-worker scope.
Direct fetch, WebSocket, popup, top navigation, form submission, and download are denied by default.
Only a one-time MessageChannel token can call the negotiated UI bridge.
Origin spoofing, token replay, oversized messages, and stale generation messages are rejected.
Suspend and dispose release bridge calls and subscriptions without affecting AppShell.

plugins.purpose: Prove the public symbol/history/realtime provider contract and stream backpressure without relying on a live exchange or credentials.
acceptance: Deterministic fixtures produce canonical symbols, capabilities, history pages, and realtime events.
Provider output enters the host ingestion/normalization path and cannot directly write cache, SQLite, GapLedger, or EventBus.
Closed, corrected, duplicate, gap, out-of-order, snapshot/delta, sequence, and resync semantics are explicit.
Credit exhaustion applies bounded backpressure and a slow provider cannot block Data Engine producers.
Crash and restart isolate the provider and do not contaminate another exchange identity.

plugins.purpose: Prove account and order contribution shapes, risk gates, idempotency, audit, and kill switch before any live credential or execution capability exists.
acceptance: Fixture accounts expose only canonical balances, positions, orders, and timestamps.
Every OrderIntent passes scope, risk, quantity, price, idempotency, and audit gates.
Duplicate submit, cancel/fill races, unknown results, reconnect, recovery, and no-lookahead are deterministic.
Revocation and the global kill switch reject the next action.
The reference plugin cannot obtain a live secret or live execution handle.

plugins.purpose: Prove that Pyne and Pine Compatibility can appear in the unified catalog while their existing protocol, release artifacts, routes, and public transports remain stable.
acceptance: The adapter preserves candlescope.script-runtime/1 and candlescope.render/1 wire contracts.
Current SDK transcript and HTTP compute, HTTP range, and indicator WebSocket canonical hashes remain unchanged.
Existing pinned Pyne and Pine bundles install and pass fresh-process semantic probes.
Registry import is explicit, previewable, reversible, and never guesses a v1-to-v2 conversion.
A stale or unavailable runtime fails closed without legacy fallback.
